newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada Thiessen sees consumer demand up.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada Thiessen sees consumer demand up.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen on Wednesday said he believed that more than a year of aggressive interest rate cuts would result in stronger consumer spending in the near future.

"I believe that it will not be long before this cumulative monetary easing of the past year encourages a resurgence in household spending," Thiessen told a luncheon in St. John's, Newfoundland, sponsored by the Newfoundland Board of Trade.

He said there were indicators that consumer demand was already on the rise, while recent surveys of investment intentions and business confidence showed that capital spending would also rise in the second half of 1996.
A rebound in domestic demand, together with continuing strong exports, will bring about a faster economic recovery in Canada in the coming months, Thiessen said.
"... the outlook is favorable for a quickening in the pace of economic activity in the months ahead," he said.
He repeated that he expects Canada's debt-to-gross domestic product ratio to start declining in 1997 and drop further in the future.
"This is good news: a decline in this ratio is essential to restore fully our financial health," Thiessen said.
